lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The skid has become the story, and Toronto can no longer disguise it as a rough patch. The Maple Leafs' 1-0 loss to Edmonton on Nov. 14 extended their losing streak to six games - a shutout defeat that left an 8-12 club 13th in the Eastern Conference, 10 points out, with only 18 points to show for the season. General manager John Chayka called the results unacceptable but publicly backed coach Jim Hiller and urged patience with Sergei Bobrovsky, whose early Toronto tenure has become its own crisis. Morgan Rielly's possible return from a lower-body injury offers some needed structure on the blue line; Kirill Marchenko remains sidelined. But this team needs saves and goals, not reassurance. Tonight in Chicago, the Blackhawks provide the next test at 7:30 p.m. ET - and a seventh straight loss would turn concern into a reckoning.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The offseason has barely opened, and Toronto already has two fires to put out: a rotation battered by injuries and a clubhouse forced to answer for Anthony Santander's conduct. General manager Ross Atkins' denunciation of Santander's anti-Islam social-media posts - calling them "extremely disappointing" - is the day's defining development. That is not a baseball footnote; it is a test of standards, accountability and whether this roster can move forward without dragging needless baggage behind it. On the field, Brendon Little offers a more useful kind of complication: after early demotions, he finished with a 2.28 ERA over his final 23.2 innings and has earned a serious look in 2027. Toronto's finished season left it at -2.0 points, but the number matters less now than the repair bill. Watch the next 40-man decisions, the pursuit of Tarik Skubal or Dustin May, and whether Toronto finally rebuilds a dependable pitching staff before camp opens March 25 at Yankee Stadium.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: A 13-point fourth-quarter lead turned into another lesson in how the Raptors keep losing games they briefly control. Sunday's 112-108 overtime defeat to the Knicks stretched Toronto's skid to four, leaving it 5-8 and fourth in the Atlantic Division, six games behind. Scottie Barnes returned from a groin strain and delivered 30 points and nine rebounds, the sort of forceful comeback this team desperately needs. But the late-game details remain ruinous: loose balls, missed switches and poor communication. RJ Barrett owned his failure to switch onto Jalen Brunson and asked frustrated fans for patience - an understandable appeal, but patience is not a defensive scheme. Kawhi Leonard remains out with left-knee swelling, and Toronto has not found a reliable answer without him. The Knicks return Tuesday at 7:30 p.m. ET, offering an immediate test of whether accountability means anything when the next close game arrives.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The Commanders survived a Thursday-night fire drill, and Luke McCaffrey's out-of-bounds kickoff gambit helped tilt the field before Washington escaped the Giants 24-21. That is not elegance; it is resourcefulness, the kind of strange little edge that keeps a season breathing. At 3-5-1, Washington sits second in the NFC East, two games back, with a one-game winning streak and no margin for sentimental optimism. Stefon Diggs supplied the late finish, while the defense still left too much grass inside - a vulnerability Cincinnati's Joe Burrow will gladly attack. The Giants win mattered because the Commanders needed it, not because it solved them. Even Sam Hartman's "Bachelor" announcement cannot distract from the football. Monday night against the Bengals is the real test: Washington must protect the middle, sharpen its coverage, and prove this was momentum rather than merely survival.

article.title: Maple Leafs Back Hiller Before Chicago Visit
paragraphs: The Leafs visit the Blackhawks tonight at 7:30 p.m. ET on TSN, with Sergei Bobrovsky projected to face Spencer Knight. Toronto is 8-12, and Morgan Rielly is day-to-day with a lower-body injury. General manager John Chayka has backed coach Jim Hiller despite the club's recent results, saying he has full confidence in Hiller and his staff.

The Jays are already looking toward March, with their regular season opening at the Yankees on Thursday, March 25, at 1:35 p.m. ET. Toronto is assessing potential acquisitions. The Raptors host the Knicks at 7:30 p.m., but Bittle and Leonard are out while McCullar Jr. is day-to-day with an illness. Washington's Commanders, 3-5-1 and second in the NFC East, next host the Bengals Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Their backup quarterback Sam Hartman has also been announced as a contestant on "The Bachelor."
